verdict.printed: Page 151 has only the Fig. 11 illustration, a head in profile with Reverence, Mysticism, Optimism and Conscientiousness labelled, and the caption 'THE RELIGIO-MORAL QUALITIES'.
verdict.evidence: The figure description and caption are page 151's own. The body, 'CHAPTER XV ... The tenth group is known as the Religio-Moral Qualities ... REVERENCE ... charla-', is printed on page 150, and none of it is on page 151. I judged from the transcriptions and did not open the images.

verdict.printed: Page 47 is a full-page plan, '10 FIGVRE.', of a star-shaped fortification. It has the letters A to M and the running head 'DE FORTIFICATION', signature F 3 and catchword EXEM-. There is no body text.
verdict.evidence: The body renders page 46's text: 'Suppose City A in this 10th Figure is far from the sea… One shall place at the mouth of the small river… a needle sluice' with '9th EXAMPLE' and 'NEW METHOD'. Page 46 prints all of this. Page 47 itself prints only 'OF FORTIFICATION', 'FIGURE 10', 'F 3' and 'EXEM-', which are rendered. The long added text, the summary and the keywords are not printed on page 47.

verdict.printed: Page 37 has only an illustration of a table with round objects labelled 拊, a four-legged stand labelled 鼓足, and the marginal 之屬. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: "The Fu drum is a vital part of the ritual ensemble... filled with husks, it produces a subdued tone" and "ritual drums are never placed directly upon the floor" are composed paragraphs that appear on none of pages 36–38. Only the headings and the 之屬 note render page 37's printed labels.

verdict.printed: Page 25 (numbered XX) has the heading 'Pro commentariis in Alciati Emblemata... a Ioanne Thvilio' and a Greek poem, 'Carmina' by Paulus Aemilius of Cadmea, praising Alciati and Thvilius.
verdict.evidence: The English 'If Virgil once declared with full mouth That farmers are fortunate...' and 'CONCERNING THE SAME' (Minos, Sanctius, Pignorius, the GERMAN) are the Latin poems by Chiocci and Langvvel printed on page 26 (XXI). None of the Greek Carmina or the heading on page 25 is rendered.

verdict.printed: Page 140 prints the end of a statute: if anyone does damage to the people, they pay double and fall into the King's mercy; the aids for knighting a son or marrying a daughter; and the 20 shillings per knight's fee. Page 139 prints the Capitulum iiii text: the peace between the King and his people, and the high men and bailiffs who attach others.
verdict.evidence: The English opens with "might survive between the King and his people... the King was taken and held in prison" and "Chapter iv.", which are printed on page 139. It then moves on to "It is provided that if anyone does damage to the people... double", which is printed on page 140. The summary and keywords are short additions.

verdict.printed: Page 17 has no continuous text, only faint sketches: architectural plans and elevations across the top, and a faint head or figure study in the middle. At most a few tiny letters or marks are visible.
verdict.evidence: "architectural diagrams at the top and a figurative drawing in the center" describes page 17's own drawings. The meta line, "previous page established the theoretical principles of hydraulics and the comparison between water and hair", is background that is not on page 16, 17 or 18.

verdict.printed: PLATE 3; photo captioned 'Kashmīri bīn-player. (Taken by Ananda K. Coomaraswamy).'; photo captioned 'Nāgasaram-players, Tanjore.'; 'P. 46'
verdict.evidence: The title and captions ('Kashmiri bīn-player', 'Nāgasaram-players, Tanjore') are rendered faithfully from page 70. However, the English also adds a meta note about Povāḍas, glossary <term> entries (e.g. 'Nāgasaram: A traditional double-reed wind instrument common in South India…'), a summary and keywords. None of these are printed on any of the three pages. The glossary entry also wrongly describes the bīn as a plucked string instrument.

verdict.printed: Page 287 is a divider page with only the italic title 'Para-biblical Literature'.
verdict.evidence: The body is 'Frag. 16 1 [...] 2 [...] his [...] 3 [...] and the waters of the flood...' through Frag. 20. None of this is printed on pages 286, 287 or 288, so it was composed for the page. The title itself is rendered correctly.

verdict.printed: Page 12: a boxed rubric paragraph on finding the terms of Septuagesima, Lent, Easter and Rogations, then a five-column table of termini (2nd moon, 14th moon of Easter, 20th Rogations, 7th Pentecost, 10th moon LXX) with Kalends/Nones/Ides dates, ogdoas/endecas headings, and a marginal 'A'.
verdict.evidence: "If you wish to know the term of Septuagesima... find out what weekday the moon is on the Kalends of January" and the table "TERM OF THE 14TH MOON OF EASTER" (page 12). The added modern-date notes (e.g. "Feb 22") and the meta paragraph are glosses and background.

verdict.printed: Page 61 has the header 'THE PAPYRUS OF ANI', plate number 12, and the labels 'Introduction to Chap. XVIII – A' and '– B'. It shows Ani and Thuthu with a priest in a panther skin, in two registers. A caption describes the vignettes and says the text is Chapters 146 and 147 (continued) plus invocations forming an introduction to Chapter 18, the Litany of Thoth.
verdict.evidence: 'THE FIFTH MANSION (CONTINUED FROM CHAPTER 147)' and 'THE SEVENTH PYLON ... Reference numbers 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 7, 6' are the page 60 headings and notes. The guardian names, such as 'The name of the doorkeeper is The Old One', and the speeches, such as 'I have come to you, O Great Council of the Gods', are printed on no page. The page 61 caption about the panther-skin priest and the two pylons is not rendered.

verdict.printed: Page 18 has three leaves of dense Tibetan text, and the transcription is empty. By position it falls between page 17 (visualization, refuge, Vajrasattva purification) and page 19 (offering to the assembly of bodies, then the guru visualization).
verdict.evidence: The English runs from the preliminaries and refuge through "OM VAJRASATTVA AH" to the three mandala offerings, ending at "assembly of the Precious Dharmakaya...". Page 19 opens with "...offer to the assembly of bodies, please accept", so this continues directly into it. The opening "Homage to... Samantabhadra" and the refuge section may be rendered loosely, but the content does not match pages 17 or 19.

verdict.printed: Page 476 (numbered 410) has the end of the Argumentum summary, the dedication heading to Charles, Landgrave of Hesse, the salutation from Leeuwenhoek, and the first words of the letter ('Sæpe numero ... accuratissimo ocu-').
verdict.evidence: The first part renders page 476's own text, e.g. 'The wonderful motion in their intestines' and 'ANTONY VAN LEEUWENHOEK, Sends many greetings'. The English then goes on with page 477's text: 'When I previously observed the web or thread of a silkworm with the help of a microscope, I judged that a thread of that kind was flat' and 'In order to be made more certain in this matter, I did not once take threads'. It also carries the rest of the opening paragraph, such as the Hereditary Prince's visit, which is printed on page 477.

verdict.printed: Nothing: page 50 is a blank page.
verdict.evidence: "GRACE, as theologians teach, is a supernatural gift, freely given by God" is a theological chapter on grace and the Council of Trent. It is printed on none of pages 49–51. Those pages hold the end of the toad tale and the tiger-story title page.

verdict.printed: Page 66 is the left half of the Tab. I engraving. It has Fig. I, VI and III, and the orbit and zodiac labels (Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpius, Sagittarius). It also has the scale of Earth semidiameters, the caption 'Genesis Cap. I. v. 1. Creatio Universi' and 'Ioh. Melchior Füeßlinus delin.'
verdict.evidence: "GENESIS Chapter 1, verse 1. The Creation of the Universe" and "Drawn by Johann Melchior Füeßlin" (both printed on page 66). The added material is minor: a meta sentence about Scheuchzer's "Sacred Physics", a gloss on "delin.", and a summary.
verdict.note: The Fig. I sphere list is described in the English but is barely legible on the scan. The English also describes the picture at length.

verdict.printed: A bookplate with a crown, a lion in a Garter collar, St George and the dragon, a helmet and an owl. The motto "Honi soit qui mal y pense" is on the collar. The handwritten shelfmark "VII. D. e. 32" is below it.
verdict.evidence: "Shame be to him who thinks evil of it" (original: "HONI SOIT QUI MAL Y PENSE") and "VII. D. e. 32", both on page 3. The added glosses are the definition of "passant guardant" and the shelfmark note, "a library shelfmark used to identify the physical location of the volume".

verdict.printed: Page 455 (numbered 427) has the continuation of the eclipse table (moments 7–15) and the text on the Benatek and Graz observations, Tycho's dispute and Mästlin, ending 'Hoc idem quidam'.
verdict.evidence: The first half renders page 455: 'The average estimated from the beginning and end for me was 1:47 1/2 hours'. The second half renders page 456: 'Regarding the estimation of the Moon's diameter through this eclipse, see Problem 12 above' and 'the sum of the semidiameters is 31' 11"'. The English also adds a short gloss and a note on 'digits'.

verdict.printed: Page 178 is a faded plate of a standing man carrying a bag. Its printed caption reads: Кн. Г. Г. Гагаринъ. Кавказскіе типы Лермонтовскихъ временъ. Тифлисскій бродячій кузнецъ.
verdict.evidence: "Prince G. G. Gagarin. Caucasian types of Lermontov's time. A wandering blacksmith from Tiflis." This translates the caption printed on page 178. The additions are small: the gloss "now Tbilisi", the "tall fur hat" gloss, and a summary and keywords.

verdict.printed: Page 31 prints the heading XI Sibylla Evropæa, a Latin paragraph on Onuphrius, Boissard, Tzetzes, Zosimus and the prophecy 'Regem Æthereum...', and a French section II with the same content.
verdict.evidence: "Onuphrius states that this eleventh Sibyl is not included in the count of ancient writers" and "This prophetess is not known among the ancient authors" both render page 31's printed text. The English also adds a meta note on continuity with page 10, footnote-style notes, a glossary of <term> entries, a summary and keywords. Examples are 'bringing the total number to twelve to match the twelve Apostles' and 'Boissardus ... published a famous book on Sibyls in 1599'. None of this is printed on page 31.

verdict.printed: Page IX: the end of a German sentence introducing Andreas Brunner's Annales, then Brunner's Latin passage on Aventinus, Otto and Albert, Siegfried of Mainz, and the Freising dispute, ending at 'publicis'.
verdict.evidence: 'we must look around for another guarantor... Andreas Brunner' and 'Aventinus possessed Albert's complete records' are both on page 306. The English also adds a <gloss> for the Annales title and a <summary> and <keywords> block, which are minor additions.

verdict.printed: A bookplate with the Latin legend "PHILOSOPHIA · HERMETICA" around a pelican emblem, and a handwritten "E" in the corner, on marbled paper.
verdict.evidence: The body renders the page's own bookplate ("HERMETIC PHILOSOPHY", original "PHILOSOPHIA · HERMETICA"; page 4). It then adds explanatory term entries and a summary that are printed on no page, e.g. "In alchemy, it represents the stage of 'rubedo' or the final perfection of the Great Work."

verdict.printed: A full-page color illustration of a man with a sword standing in a lotus pond with white mist, plus a red seal. It has no printed text or caption.
verdict.evidence: The body opens "The Lord of Koriyama was not the only one affected; his wife and child were also struck down" and ends with the yamabushi's speech "plant the lotus, not only...". This is the text printed on page 470, headed "IPPAI ATTACKS THE CHILDREN". Page 471 shows only the picture.

verdict.printed: Page 98: woodcut of a pepper plant, then 11 lines of Latin verse on pepper (hot and dry, three kinds, black pepper aiding digestion, poisonous bites, chest ailments, periodic fever), with marginal labels.
verdict.evidence: "It has three types: the white, the long, and the black" with margin "Three types of pepper" (page 115). The additions are short notes, such as the humoral-theory gloss and the term glosses, plus the meta and summary.

verdict.printed: Page 165 (numbered 117, header 'De Metempsychosi') has the end of §8 on metempsychosis and the serpent image, then the start of §9 on material souls, ending mid-word at 'reso-'.
verdict.evidence: The English opens with page 165's 'it took its origin, through magnetism…' and 'coiled serpent'. It then runs on past the page's last printed words ('reso-') into page 166's text: 'The soul is not hidden in the earth… caput mortuum… For we see that from dead and putrefied'.

verdict.printed: Nothing visible: all three scans (358, 359, 360) render as blank white pages.
verdict.evidence: The body is a picture description, "Botanical plate featuring multiple specimens of fungi... clusters of small, pale, gilled mushrooms", plus "Reference to Plate 486" and a summary naming Mycena. None of this is visible on page 359 or on 358 or 360. The scan is blank, so the plate number and the genus guess come from the machine transcription, not from printed text.

verdict.printed: Page 119 has the title 旄, the caption 干旄, and the margin text 欽定四庫全書, 詩經疏義會通 and page number 五九. It also has an illustration of a dragon-headed staff with a hanging cord and four tassels.
verdict.evidence: The English has "Mao Ceremonial banner staff" and "Ganmao" for the title and caption (page 119), plus a description of the dragon-head finial and four tassels. The added glosses ("Shield and banner; a dance ritual", "ancient court dances") and the "woodblock print" meta line are minor background. "Possibly a jade disc or bell" is a guess about the picture. The summary's claim that the pole is a "ceremonial banner pole" used in dances is likewise an unprinted gloss.

verdict.printed: Page 539 (xlviii) is a two-column INDEX GRAMMATICUS running from 'ficatu' through the entries Constrata, Consuefacit, Consuetudine, Consul, Consulam, Consulares and Consulatum, ending at 'Consulta et decreta... ut de'.
verdict.evidence: 'Constrata telis omnia [all things strewn with weapons] J 101' and 'Senatus a Bestia consultus est [the Senate was consulted by Bestia] J 28' are both printed on page 539. The English stops mid-entry at 'Romæ Se', so the rest of column 2 is not rendered. The added glosses are word-for-word translations, not extra content.

verdict.printed: Page 687 (XXXIIII) is Latin body text on iron, from 'dei patientia inductus' to 'Quedam'. It covers iron's varieties, tempering, the magnet, rust-proofing and the start of the medicinal uses.
verdict.evidence: 'Iron mines are found almost everywhere... the island of Elba' and 'Dinocrates, the architect of Alexander' render page 687's own text. The English then appends a short block, '<translation page="688">... are healed by burning. Specifically, however, [it is used for] the bites of a mad dog', which is printed on page 688. It also adds a summary and keywords, and mentions a decorative initial D that is not on the scan.

verdict.printed: Page 53 has the header 'CREATION SERIES, TABLET VII. PLATE XL.', the museum number '91139 + 93073.', the label 'OBVERSE (cont.).' and a hand-drawn cuneiform facsimile with stippled damage. It has no English prose.
verdict.evidence: 'Asaru-alim, whose weight is heavy in the assembly of the gods... Tutu, who effects their restoration' is a composed translation of Marduk's names. It is printed on none of the three pages, which carry only cuneiform drawings. Only the header, museum number and 'OBVERSE (Continued)' label match page 53's printed text.

verdict.printed: Only the title 宋太宗像 (Portrait of Emperor Taizong of Song) above a woodcut bust of an official in a winged futou cap and round-collared robe.
verdict.evidence: The body is composed commentary printed on none of the three pages: "Song tradition evolved them into these long, stiff extensions to prevent court officials from whispering" and the Taizu "yellow robe"/"cup of wine" note. The running header "Humanity: Volume Three / Page Eleven" is printed on page 25 (人物三卷 十二), not page 24. The title itself is rendered as "Portrait of Emperor Taizong of Song".

verdict.printed: Page 517 (header IN VERREM) has Latin text from 'dederint: post uidebitur…' through the Cybea ship, Veliae, Hortensius and the old laws against senators building ships, ending 'ne illa que'. Its catchword is 'q='.
verdict.evidence: The body begins 'Finally, did you never think that this would be criminal or invidious for you? To have a cargo ship built…', which translates 'Postremo tu tibi hoc nunquam criminosum…' on page 518. It goes on past page 518 with Feciales, Taurominitanians and the treaties. Only the header 'AGAINST VERRES' and the catchword match page 517.

verdict.printed: Page 4 has a pasted bookplate with the printed legend PHILOSOPHIA HERMETICA around a pelican-in-her-piety emblem. It also has pencil shelfmarks: 281, Cod. Ms 876, Heck/Cat/Par, Q, and Q Mat lc 4435.
verdict.evidence: The English renders "Hermetic Philosophy" and the pelican emblem from page 4. It then adds unprinted commentary: "The letter Q was a common mark used by the firm of Bernard Quaritch...", the glossary entries on Codex, Shelfmark and Hermes Trismegistus, and the claim that the manuscript passed through private and commercial collections. The opening meta also refers back to the Hamilton Palace provenance on page 3, which is not printed on page 4.
verdict.added_note: The body mostly renders page 4's own content, but the added background, glossary and speculation amount to paragraphs.

verdict.printed: Page 60 (Liber II, sig. d ij) prints Cicero's Academica text from 'uideare mentitus' through Chrysippus, Carneades, the dreamers, drunkards and madmen, Ennius, Alcmeo and Iliona, and ends mid-sentence at 'qualis tandem fuit affinis tuus'.
verdict.evidence: The English opens with 'You seem to have lied. But to come to matters that are clearer...' and runs through Iliona (page 60). It then continues with 'Catulus Tuditanus... Hercules in Euripides... Apollo the long-haired stretches His golden bow... Diana casts a torch', which is printed on page 61. It also includes an invented meta note about 'skepticism and the nature of perception'.

verdict.printed: Page 540 (Book X): the extemporal speaker's attention, shame and praise as spurs, the difficulty and training of extempore facility with Antipater of Sidon and Archias, and declaimers who start without preparing. It has marginal notes, including the Pudor and Facultas extemporalis notes, and ends with 'Declamatores quosdam peruersa ducit ambitio, vt exposita controuersia'.
verdict.evidence: The body begins 'in this kind, I entirely accept this brief annotation... That which Lenas advises, I dislike' and goes on to 'Book X. I. Preface, and on speaking appropriately... Socrates'. None of this is printed on pages 557–559. Only the margin notes ('Modesty.', 'Extemporaneous facility is difficult...', 'Meditation must be applied.') match page 558.

verdict.printed: Page 231 is a plate of six figures (a pump mechanism, joints and a water wheel). It carries the header 'Architecture Hydraulique, Livre III, Chapitre 4, Planche 4', the title 'Développemens d'une Machine exécutée à Nymphenbourg' and the margin note '1ere Partie, Tome II, Pl. 12'.
verdict.evidence: 'Detailed Plans of a Machine constructed at Nymphenburg' and 'HYDRAULIC ARCHITECTURE, BOOK III. Chapter 4. Plate 4.' are both printed on page 231. The English adds a palace-background note, term glosses, a summary and keywords that are not printed on any of the three pages.

verdict.printed: English translation, header M. CORNELIUS FRONTO, page 65: the purple cloak and Cleanthes and Diogenes lines, then section 13 (Immortal Gods, Comitium, Rostra, Tereus and Lycurgus, eloquence, the vine, Minerva and Mercury), plus three footnotes.
verdict.evidence: "against your will you must put on the purple cloak... Diogenes the Cynic not only earned no money" is printed on page 77. The stored English stops there, followed by a long run of dots. It leaves out section 13 and the footnotes, and it adds a meta line about Fronto urging Marcus to keep his role as an orator, which is not printed on page 77.

verdict.printed: Page 279 is Latin prose from the end of Apollonius's speech. It closes the Stesichorus palinode appeal, then gives the Thespion argument about the Pythian temple, with the wax-and-feather temple, the golden birds, the gifts and statues, and Polygnotus's painting. It ends mid-word at 'ostendere il-'.
verdict.evidence: The first part renders page 279, e.g. 'You have brought forward, moreover, O Thespion...'. From 'desiring, as I think, [to show] the wealth of the barbarians' onward it renders page 280, as in 'Old women with their heads wrapped in flour-sieves...' and 'I love modesty of speech'. None of that is printed on page 279.

verdict.printed: Page 278 (printed 242) has the header 'NO. XXI. SERIES d. babbar-dim é-la RAW. IV XI'. It then gives transliterated Sumerian/Akkadian lines 53-57, a 'Reverse.' heading, and SBH p. 63 reverse lines 1-25 with Sumerian and Akkadian text. A footnote 1 at the bottom says 'Probably both tablets ended on the obv. with the same line.'
verdict.evidence: The English keeps the header and lines 53-57 ('53 e-de-bi gul-a | ni-gul-gul-[e]', page 278). It adds invented glosses such as 'its foundation destroyed' and a 'Continuity' note about 'Exalted Hero of the World'. Reverse lines 1-25 are replaced by a long run of dots, and footnote 1 is missing.

verdict.printed: Page 3 has the handwritten number 9272 (the transcription reads 9274), an "H", a pasted label with the circular text PHILOSOPHIA HERMETICA around a pelican-and-shield emblem, and a crossed-out number 10720.
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 3's own marks and label: "9274", "H", "The text Hermetic Philosophy ... is printed in a circle around a central oval", and the crossed-out "10720". It then adds a block of background: the pelican as "a traditional symbol of self-sacrifice and the alchemical process", plus four <term> glossary entries on Hermetic Philosophy, Pelican in its piety, Saltire and Heraldry, and a summary. None of this is printed on page 3.

verdict.printed: Latin dialogue between Polycarpus and Callistus: Polycarpus is won over, then mocks scholastics. The Cicero references (Tusculans, On Divination, Democritus) follow, and Callistus agrees to recount the Platonists' views.
verdict.evidence: "You would scarcely believe, Callistus, how much I have been soothed by your entire speech..." and "It is a discussion about Democritus, I believe" are both printed on page 25. The glosses, the <note> and the closing summary are small additions.

verdict.printed: Page 29 (header 'The Fifth Chapter'): Sanskrit verses 19-27 listing the sacred sites and the groups of eight (Sthanu group, divine origins, yoga group) and the names at the Purusha, Vidya and Kala levels.
verdict.evidence: "...with the 'Small Canal' kanakhala, the 'Open Space' nakhala, the 'Field of the Kurus' kurukshetra, and Gaya... (19)" is verse 19 on page 109, and the English runs through verse 27, 'Shrikantha are situated in Time'. Only the meta note about Bhairava, Kedara and Mahakala, from verses 17-18 on page 108, comes from a neighbouring page, and the translated names carry glosses.

verdict.printed: Page 69 (image 515), 'De rebus restituendis': the end of the argument on causa sine qua non, covering the resolution, the objection and Aristotle's definition of cause, and replies to the first two arguments, ending at 'erat' (catchword).
verdict.evidence: 'It is answered to the arguments brought forth in the opposition to the first opinion' and 'TO THE SECOND, in which the matter of given counsel is touched upon' both appear on page 515, at the bottom of the image. The machine transcription is cut off after 'damnum ali', but the scan shows this text. The English ends with a stray '<translation pag' fragment.

verdict.printed: Title page of Jordan's De eo quod Divinum aut Supernaturale est in morbis, with an engraved border of humor and element panels. It lists the four appended items, carries the Augustine quotation, and gives the Frankfurt imprint of Schönwetter, 1651.
verdict.evidence: "Concerning that which is Divine or Supernatural in the diseases of the human body" and "At the expense of Johann Gottfried Schönwetter. 1651." (both page 1). The notes on Conring, Augustine and the humors, and the summary, are short glosses.

verdict.printed: Page 508 (scan 522): running head 'Cautiones, &c. I. Quoad tactum', then the end of the kiss argument, Cantipratanus's anecdotes of the virgin and the priest and of the virgin and the soldier, and the opening of the next paragraph, which breaks off at 'dimitti' with the catchword 'à'.
verdict.evidence: The English renders all of page 522, but then continues with 'by sacred men; with the laws of the age trampled underfoot... Paulinus says of Saint Ambrose: "When he had grown up..."'. That text is printed on page 523 (509), and the right-hand strip on the 522 scan is only the edge of that next page.

verdict.printed: Page 245 prints only the running header 'The Code of Hammurabi / Plate XV', the heading 'COLUMN X.', a cuneiform facsimile in two columns, and line numbers 5–45. It has no English text.
verdict.evidence: 'Law 157: If a man, after the death of his father, has lain in the bosom of his mother, they shall burn both of them' is not printed on pages 244, 245 or 246. Page 245 holds only the cuneiform facsimile, and the other two pages are blank. The English body is a translation of Laws 155–159 composed for the page, with added notes and a summary.

verdict.printed: Page 271 (folio 130, Book VIII): the end of the passage on mountain springs and plains, the heading 'De aqua hymbrium, Caput II', and the start of the rainwater chapter, ending mid-sentence at 'spūs, & impe-'.
verdict.evidence: Page 271's text is rendered, from 'and the mountains themselves have their own shadows' to 'Aer autem cum ruit trudens'. The English then goes on with text printed only on page 272: 'it makes the spirits, the impetus, and the increasing waves of the winds', 'One may also take an example from baths', 'drips onto the heads of the bathers', and 'In India, there are...'.

verdict.printed: Page 400 (numbered 196) has the end of Cicero's letter 1 and the start of letter 2 to Atticus. It covers the inheritance, the dowry, the money in Asia and Chrysippus's news, and breaks off at "mi-" (catchword "nor").
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 400 through "...who seem to be in the same situation, it would seem to be by my own fault". It then goes on with page 401's text: "I have sent the courier back to you late", "70,000 sesterces", the heading "CICERO SENDS GREETINGS TO ATTICUS. 3", and "Regarding the Kalends of July", ending "the administration" (page 401, "admini-").

verdict.printed: Page 29 is a map of the western Huguang region with place labels such as 房, 竹溪, 歸, 施南, 施州, 辰州, 武岡, 會同, 常德, 靖州 and 沅江源. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: The English lists labels like "Jingzhou, Zhijiang, Songzi, Yidu, Changyang, Guizhou, Badong, Jianshi, Shinan, Shizhou" (page 29 map). It also adds a "Mountains and Waterways" line naming "Yangtze River, Han River", which are not clearly printed on the page. Most of the English renders page 29's own map labels, and page 28 and page 30 contribute nothing. The additions are only a minor gloss.

verdict.printed: Page 50 is a full-page woodcut landscape with only the title 九日山圖 (Mount Jiuri illustration) in a cartouche at top right. There is no body text.
verdict.evidence: The body begins "Near the Shrine of the Immortal Jin and the Elixir Stove, there stands the Hundred-Zhang Rock... Staff of Goosefoot Spring... Pure Source Spring". This renders the text printed on page 49 (如金眞人祠及丹竈上有百丈石山…). The English adds a few glosses, such as "popular destination for visitors... seeking recreation". The title "Illustration of Mount Jiuri" is the only rendering of page 50's own text.

verdict.printed: Page 324 (Cap. XVIII commentary) discusses the fading of the names of the wicked, the blessing of children, and the pious who die childless, such as Abel and the Prophets. It ends with the catchword 'non'.
verdict.evidence: The English opens 'they are not always the heirs of paternal piety, as is apparent from the sons of Samuel…', which renders the start of page 325 ('non sunt semper paternæ pietatis hæredes'). Nothing from page 324 is rendered. After the end of page 325 the English goes on with 'The ignorance of God is certainly the cause of iniquity… Psalm 14… Gal. 6' and a 'CHAPTER XIX' heading, which are printed on none of the three pages.

verdict.printed: Page 122 (Justin, Book XII): Antipater's letters about the deaths of Agis, Alexander of Epirus and Zopyrion; Agis's revolt; Alexander of Epirus's departure for Italy, the oracles of Dodona, and the start of his war with the Appuli. It ends at the catchword 'ma'.
verdict.evidence: The English opens 'shortly thereafter, he made peace and friendship with their king. For at that time, the city of the Appuli was Brundisium...', which is page 123's text ('breui post tempore pacem... Brunduſium'). Nothing from page 122 (Agis, Antipater, Dodona) appears. The English then runs on to Thalestris, Persian dress and the banquets, which are on none of the three pages.

verdict.printed: Page 386 has the running head 'A KEY TO PHYSIC,' and the title 'Decumbiture of John Till Adams, M.D. late of Bristol'. It shows two square astrological charts. The first is captioned as born 13th Nov. 3h. 20m. in Morning, 1748, 'A well-known Character resident in Bristol'. The second is captioned as taken ill with a Putrid Fever, 12th Feb. 2h. 8m. in Morning, 1786, Bristol.
verdict.evidence: 'BORN November 13th, 3:20 a.m., 1748. A well-known figure who resided in Bristol' and 'Taken ill with a PUTRID FEVER... February 12th, 2:08 a.m., 1786. Bristol' render the chart captions printed on page 511. The added material is the <note> glosses, the glossary, and the meta and summary lines, which are not printed on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 43 prints the running title 欽定西清硯譜, the page number 二十三, the caption 宋端石海天硯正面圖, and a woodcut of the inkstone front with a pavilion plaque and small carved labels.
verdict.evidence: "Front View of the Song Dynasty Duan Stone 'Sea and Sky' Inkstone" and "Imperially Commissioned Catalogue of Xiqing Inkstones" render the caption and running title printed on page 43. The rest is a description of the picture. The back-view caption and the Su Dongpo inscription from page 44 are not included.

verdict.printed: Page 33 has the title 紅花菜 (Honghuacai), the running header 救荒本草, the folio number, and a full-page line drawing of a leafy flowering plant with thistle-like heads. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: "The leaves are similar to willow leaves... resemble the Japanese Elecampane (Xuanfuhua)" appears on no page. Page 34 has different content (safflower, thorny leaves, dye), so this paragraph is composed. Only the title and header are rendered from page 33. The sweet flavour and blanching with oil and salt echo page 34's 救飢 line, but loosely.

verdict.printed: Page 526 prints the margin note 'Sup causam mixtionis est discretionis causa', then the text on God's sublimity and face, the causes of mixing and of distinction, the fifth life, and the start of the list of lives (first concupiscible, second irascible...), ending mid-word at 'irasabi'.
verdict.evidence: The English opens with page 526's text ('And that sublimity of God communicates itself to all'). It then continues with 'The fifth is contemplative, proper to the mind... Therefore, having dismissed the four, he proposes to treat...' and 'the usual precept of Plato', which are printed on page 527 ('Quinta contemplatiua propria mentis', 'Hec solita illa Platonis preceptio').

verdict.printed: Page 49 is a facsimile plate with only the headers "FOLIO 17 (recto)" and "FOLIO 17 (verso)" printed, above two photographs of the manuscript leaves. No transcribed or translated text is printed.
verdict.evidence: "That object weighs more which departs further from the center of the world" and "If an equilateral triangle be circumscribed by a circle..." are not printed on pages 48, 49 or 50. They are a composed transcription and translation of the manuscript image, plus invented notes and a vocab list. Only the folio headers match page 49's printed text.

verdict.printed: Page 345 is a colour plate of the Sifilet bird of paradise on a branch. The only printed text is the caption 'Le Sifilet. Pl. 6.'
verdict.evidence: "The Sifilet. Pl. 6." translates the caption on page 345. The picture description is accurate. The one addition is "or the Greater Parotia" with the original "Parotia sefilata", which is attributed to the caption but is not printed on page 345.

verdict.printed: Page 33 has only two captions, 戈氅 and 儀鍠氅, above two illustrations of a dagger-axe and a halberd, each with a hanging streamer.
verdict.evidence: "The Dagger-Axe Banner" and "The Ceremonial Halberd Banner" (page 33) render the two captions. The added notes are not printed on any page. They include the "Gechang" and "Yihuangchang" notes, the claim that the yihuang were used by "Luanqi (Imperial Chariot) guards", the meta line about "Volume 11... Page 18", and the summary paragraph.

verdict.printed: Page 8 has only the title 人參 and a woodcut of two ginseng plants, with no body text.
verdict.evidence: "Ginseng" header and the illustration description, both on page 8. The added "human root" shape and "most revered of all herbs" paragraph, the "high-quality example of pre-modern Chinese botanical illustration" note, and the Panax ginseng, Bencao and woodblock commentary are on none of the pages. The meta note about Sweet Flag is also invented, since page 7's text does not end on a pungent flavor when chewed.

verdict.printed: Page 6 has only a pasted-in Gdańsk bookplate: arms with two lions, captioned EX BIBLIOTHECA SENATVS GEDANENSIS. Faint show-through of the page 5 title is visible at the top.
verdict.evidence: "FROM THE LIBRARY OF THE COUNCIL OF GDAŃSK" is the page 6 caption. Most of the body, "ON SECRET CHARACTERS IN LETTERS... BY GIAMBATTISTA DELLA PORTA... AT MONTBÉLIARD... 1593" with the Minerva emblem, is the page 5 title page, not page 6.

verdict.printed: Page 146 (printed no. 101) carries Demosthenes' De Corona: the defence plan, the 'influx of traitors' passage, Philip's advantage, and the question of which camp Athens should have joined. It ends mid-sentence with 'ἐὰν... μὴ τῶν αὑτοῦ συμμάχων'.
verdict.evidence: The English opens with page 146's 'Having arranged the matters written here... I will omit nothing willingly'. It then runs on to 'But I return to that point. What was it fitting for the city to do...' and 'raised in Pella, a place that was then obscure and small', which are printed on page 147 (ἀλλ' ἐκεῖσε ἐπανέρχομαι; τῷ ἐν Πέλλῃ τραφέντι). The 'note' glosses are minor additions.

verdict.printed: Page 363 (numbered 143) prints the end of the Origen argument (ipsa prior est quàm intelligentia…), the heading 'Obiectio Epicureorum', Cap. 7, and the start of the reply about incorruptible and corruptible bodies, which breaks off at 'ex quatuor'.
verdict.evidence: The English omits the opening Origen paragraph on 363. It renders the Cap. 7 start ('Dicaearchus or some Epicurean will struggle against these things…', 363). It then runs on into 364's text ('There are also middle bodies… Such will be our souls', 364) and well past 364's last word ('stel-'), for example 'We have seen three bodies and three spirits… Anaxagoras… θνητὸς αἰὼν μέρος ἔχει θεοῦ τινος', which is on none of the three pages.

verdict.printed: Page 7 is a full-page, high-contrast plate of a Tibetan painting with a dark border and many small figures. It has no printed text, title or caption.
verdict.evidence: "The composition centers on a primary figure seated in a meditative posture on a throne" describes the picture on page 7. The background glosses, such as "Bodhisattvas <note>enlightened beings who help others reach enlightenment</note>" and the identification as a "Refuge Tree", are minor additions. The caption "Ts'ogs-śin or Assembly of Divinities" is printed on page 8 and is not rendered here.

verdict.printed: Page 148 is a plate with only two tiny captions, 'Frutex &c.' and 'Anguis &c.', under the picture of a berried shrub with a green snake.
verdict.evidence: 'The French Mulberry... Frutex foliis serratis, floribus albis, baccis tyriis' and 'usually measuring about twelve inches... The belly is white' appear on no page. Page 149 describes the snake and shrub differently, with red berries and a turned-up nose. The English never renders 'Frutex &c.' or 'Anguis &c.'.

verdict.printed: Only the title 'ЭПИЛОГЪ.' (Epilogue) on an otherwise blank page.
verdict.evidence: The body 'Seven years had passed... The agitated sea of European historical life had subsided into its shores' renders page 232's opening. The title 'EPILOGUE' is rendered from page 231. Paragraphs such as 'In Russia, too, a reaction took place... cast a stone at Alexander I' are printed on none of the three pages.

verdict.printed: Page 128 shows a dark pebbled cover with a library barcode (D 000 012 ... 6) and a green label reading "NEX" (INDEX, cut off) on the right edge. It has no book text.
verdict.evidence: "<insert>D 000 012 158 6</insert>" and "<insert>NEX</insert>" render page 128's own labels. The notes calling them a modern library barcode and a classification stamp are minor glosses.

verdict.printed: Page 132 (book p. 120): end of the capital-crime sentence (drowning in the Nile), Bedawee blood-revenge, retaliation and fines for wounds, and the start of the theft law, ending at 'ordains that this'.
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 132's text, then goes on with page 133's content: 'less than a quarter of a deenár (a gold coin)', the Sháfe'ee/Hanafee penalties, the kurbág, adultery and stoning, and the Kur-án quotation (page 133). It then continues past page 133 with 'the testimony required of one of them shall be that he swear four times by God…', the verse 2 fornication penalty, and 'Drunkenness was punished by the Prophet with flogging' (none of which is on pages 131–133).

verdict.printed: Page 2 shows a drawing of an open book with a stippled left page marked A and a plain right page marked B. Below it is the French text 'Contraste insuffisant' and the code 'NF Z 43-120-14'.
verdict.evidence: 'Insufficient contrast' and 'NF Z 43-120-14' (page 2). The English also adds glosses and a summary, such as 'a specific French industrial standard for micrography and document conservation', which are not printed on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 205 prints only the header 'DELL' ARTIFICIOSE MACHINE.', page number 84, signature 'l iij', title 'FIGVRE LIIII.' and the engraving of the hydraulic machine with letters; no body text.
verdict.evidence: 'With the mechanism of this other kind of machine, one likewise makes water rise from any low place to a height by means of a channel' is the French text of CHAP. LIIII on page 204; page 205 has only the figure, header and title 'FIGURE LIV'.

verdict.printed: Page 52 is an illustration of a two-masted oared ship. It carries the title 八槳船 (Eight-Oared Ship), the running head 武備志卷百十 (Wubei Zhi, juan 110), and a small margin note about the ship's size.
verdict.evidence: "# The Eight-Oared Ship" and "Treatise on Armament Technology, Volume 117" render the title and running head on page 52. The glossary entries and the background notes ("Compiled by Mao Yuanyi in 1621", "most comprehensive military encyclopedia", "ideal for scouting, pursuit") are not printed on any of the three pages.

verdict.printed: Page 2 is a plain brown leather cover with no text except the digital watermark '© Dharmartha Trust J&K. Digitized by eGangotri'.
verdict.evidence: The body ('physical front cover... dark brown material, likely leather... visible grain and significant staining and wear') describes page 2's own cover image. The one added line is 'Following the library identification label... the manuscript "The Victory of the Illustrious Ranavira"', and that title comes from page 1's label.

verdict.printed: Page 59 is a woodcut diagram of a walled city. The characters 郭 (top right) and 城 (centre) are the only text. A double wall with gate towers sits inside a river and mountains.
verdict.evidence: "Outer Rampart — Guo 郭" and "Inner City Wall — Cheng 城" render the two printed labels on page 59. The notes on the dual-wall system and the 'Page 31' heading are extra, but only a gloss and a short background paragraph.

verdict.printed: Page 17 is the 'Figura Divina' diagram. It has the title, the Triune God emblem, Hyle chaos, Philosophia and Chimia, and the alchemical stage circles. Left and right columns of German and Latin annotations run down the sides, with margin notes and a 4 Elementa symbol.
verdict.evidence: 'Nothing more is, in time, nothing more. God becomes Nature.' and 'Water was my life in the beginning, that is also my death forevermore' are both printed on page 17. The title 'Divine Figure... The Triune God' is also on page 17. The English adds only a short summary and keywords.

verdict.printed: Page 248 is a photograph of the Sri Sri Bhavatarini shrine, with only the caption 'Sri Sri Bhavatarini' printed below it.
verdict.evidence: The body begins '...there would be no difficulty in the worship and service of the Divine Mother even if Ramkumar were unable...' and goes on to Kenaram Bhattacharya's initiation and Ramkumar's death. That is the text printed on page 247 (page number 134), not on 248. The caption and image description do render page 248's own content.

verdict.printed: Page 70 has only the woodcut of a thorny-stemmed lobed-leaf tree, the title 刺楸, the running header 三才圖會卷之草木八 and the folio 廿五. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: The body says "grows in Haizhou... bark is white... branches densely covered in sharp prickles... used to treat wind-dampness and foot qi". None of this is on pages 69, 70 or 71. Page 71 does give bitter, slightly cold and non-toxic, but it names the 梓 white bark, the Shijing and Lu Ji, and says nothing about Haizhou, thorns, wind-dampness or foot qi. The title, header and folio are rendered, though the folio is given as "Thirty-Five" instead of 廿五 (25).

verdict.printed: Handwritten shelfmark 'ZZZ.1.', a pasted hand-colored bookplate marked 'A' with the watermark-like legend 'PHILOSOPHIA HERMETICA' around an oval showing a pelican, an ouroboros and a shield with roses.
verdict.evidence: "HERMETIC PHILOSOPHY" with note 'original: "PHILOSOPHIA HERMETICA"' and 'the letter "A" written in the top left corner' (page 3). The added material is glosses and background: the '1714 edition' remark and the term definitions.

verdict.printed: Page 413 is a fragment of hieroglyph columns 13–18 with the column numbers and the label 'CHAP. CXXV'. It has no English text and no caption.
verdict.evidence: 'O He-Whose-Head-Is-Turned-Back, who comes forth from Sais, I have not been unchaste with a woman' is a composed list of judges and sins. It is not printed on 412, 413 or 414. Only 'CHAPTER 125' matches the printed 'CHAP. CXXV'.

verdict.printed: Page 285 (numbered 109) has the end of the Symposium note (ninth Olympiad, Athenaeus, Casaubon), the list Hiero, Revenues, Horses, Horsemanship, Hunting and Epistles, the Periplus note, the Annius forgery note, and a woodcut tailpiece.
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 285's list and notes ("Hiero, or, On Kingship... Periplus... Equivocations... Annius"). It then adds "CHAP. VIII. His writings... Dionysius of Halicarnassus says that Xenophon was a diligent imitator of Herodotus... Cyropaedia... Anabasis", which is printed on page 284.

verdict.printed: Page 358's scan (running head 'ALEXANDER SEVERUS', page 279) is Lampridius on Alexander Severus: Claudian, daily routine, baths and meals, chapter XXXI on correspondence and reading.
verdict.evidence: 'Maximinus was first called Augustus by the army, without a decree of the Senate' and 'a faction prepared against him by a certain Magnus' come from the Maximini Duo text. That text is not on any of the three scans, which all show Lampridius on Alexander Severus. The English does not render the Claudian or bath-and-meals passages that are on page 358.

verdict.printed: Nothing is printed. The page shows only the marbled-paper board and half-leather spine of the binding, with tiny faded spine labels.
verdict.evidence: "The manuscript is preserved in a classic half-leather binding... tan and brown marbled paper" describes the cover picture on page 260. The added glosses on binding terms and the sentence about the shelfmark UBN 2598 a (page 259) are minor extras.

verdict.printed: An engraved plate with two framed scenes (a lion-shaped couch with a figure and canopic jars, labelled T and M), the header 'To. I. Pag. 86.' and the caption 'La durée du repos d'Horus.'
verdict.evidence: The body renders 'Does the Egyptian farmer seek the Heaven of the most perfect rest? ... Let us convert the sign of the Lion into a bed of rest', which is the running text printed on page 170 (repeated on page 172), not on the plate page 171. The added meta and summary are also not printed on 171. The caption 'The duration of the rest of Horus' does appear on 171.

verdict.printed: Page 30 (Livy, Lib. I, header 'LIB. I.'): Latin text from 'adeptas: nec eis Iberum Hispaniam peti' to 'Erat in medio riuus paltis utrinque clau-'.
verdict.evidence: The English renders page 176 in full, then continues with page 177's text. Examples are 'he said to his brother Mago: This will be the place for you to hold' and 'Sempronius... led out all his cavalry'. It ends with 'the sharper force of the cold blew upon them', which is not printed on any of the three pages.

verdict.printed: Page xii (17): header ABBREVIATIONS, then four notation rules: unknown number of letters lost (- - -), round brackets for supplied letters, angular brackets for supplied letters where there is no lacuna, and square brackets for letters conjecturally omitted.
verdict.evidence: The English opens with 'Ox. = the Oxford facsimiles… Nap. = the Naples edition… N.B. In the Naples editions the word column…', which is printed on page 16, not 17. It then renders page 17's 'Letters conjecturally supplied to fill a gap are enclosed by round brackets, thus, (a)'. It also adds short editorial notes, such as the Hayter note and the lacuna note.

verdict.printed: Page 91 (printed 87) has a five-line Latin paragraph beginning 'dium ferentes. Ipsa enim quæ in Alpha apparet Recta Linea...', then a rotated table in six columns. The columns are headed Alpha/Omega, Cross and M, and list the correspondences from 'Existens ante Elementa' to 'Rex Regum Vbique', plus a second set of columns.
verdict.evidence: 'For that very Straight Line which appears in the Alpha is homologous to that part of the Cross...' and the table 'Mortal Adam... Born in a Stable... Beginning/Middle/End' are both printed on page 91. The added glosses are minor: the note that the sentence completes the previous page ('most sweet and most healing remedy'), the notes on omologa/Anatomiæ/Hyle, and the meta and summary lines. The summary's claim that the page 'concludes the alchemical instructions for the Monad vessels' is background that is not on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 3 has a handwritten inscription, "d. w. / Diß ist ein Inventarium bei der pfarr. / Zu sarneren. und bethen.", a pencil "M folio", and a pasted Philosophia Hermetica bookplate showing a pelican.
verdict.evidence: "This is an inventory for the parish at Sarnen and for devotions." renders the handwritten lines on page 3. The extra material is background glosses, such as the pelican as a Christian and alchemical symbol and Sarnen as a Swiss town. Nothing from page 4's title (Langens Biblisches Licht und Recht) appears.

verdict.printed: Engraved plate: header 'Tom. VII', 'Pag. 418', 'Tav. 4', signed 'J. Zambelli fecit', with Figs. 17-21 and their letter labels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G) on a scene of experimenters at a table.
verdict.evidence: 'Volume VII. Page 418. Plate 4.' and 'Created by J. Zambelli' render the page 69 header and signature. The figure labels are also rendered. The English then adds Galvani biography, 'warm-blooded' mammal claims, a glossary, a summary and keywords, none of which are printed on page 69.
